newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds slip in quiet trade, follow U.S.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds slip in quiet trade, follow U.S.

text.p: Argentine bonds were slightly lower late Monday as the market tracked U.S. Treasuries first higher and then lower through the session.
"The bond market is looking for support levels and is continuing on its upward channel in the medium-term," said an analyst. Activity was thin as the market calmed down after Friday's surge.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 fell $0.05 to 126.30, while Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 slipped 1/8 to 90-3/8.
With no clear outlook yet established for U.S. Treasuries because of uncertainty over U.S. monetary policy, analysts said Argentine bond markets were set to remain nervous.

"Until the panorama is clearer, we continue to predict a volatile market in which one should adopt a more defensive position," said analysts at C&E Consultores in an investor note. In the money markets, call money rates rose to 6.18
